keyQuestions.text: Q1. What unset speckit.worktreeBase and removed the reaper's daemon handling, and does anything still create worktrees under .worktrees/ by default?
Q2. What is git 2.50.1's documented fsmonitor daemon lifecycle on macOS, and how do fsmonitor.socketDir, idle shutdown and git fsmonitor--daemon stop behave when the daemon is wedged?
Q3. Is event overload the real cause of the hang, or is there a known daemon deadlock in this git version, for example around --ipc-threads or the cookie-file handshake?
Q4. Which call sites in the repo's hooks and scripts run git without a timeout, and which of them should opt out of fsmonitor?
Q5. What is the safest default: fsmonitor on with worktrees outside the checkout, or fsmonitor off for the main checkout and on per worktree?

keyFindings.text: `speckit.worktreeBase` is local-only configuration: `git config --show-origin --get-regexp` prints it nowhere for this checkout (only `file:.git/config core.fsmonitor true` and `core.untrackedcache true`), and no commit can unset an unversioned `.git/config` key. The regression was not a code revert of the relocation policy; the policy record simply is not in the repository. [SOURCE: git config --show-origin output, this session]

Because the reaper documents "never signals a process", re-adding daemon killing inside `worktree-reaper.sh` would break a published contract rather than restore one; a fsmonitor reap belongs in its own entry point (or in a `--reap-fsmonitor` sibling) whose invariant can be stated separately. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/README.md:168] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md:85]

Eleven `git fsmonitor--daemon run --detach --ipc-threads=8` processes are alive as of 09:22Z, the oldest started Oct 11 18:29:55 (PID 1157, 16 days), and every one of them is Xcode's `git-core`. Nothing in the repo starts, stops, or bounds them: the reaper is a manual CLI, and its published invariant is now "never signals a process". [SOURCE: ps -Ao pid,lstart,command output, this session] [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/README.md:168]

Nothing else in the repo opts this checkout out of the in-checkout default. `.worktrees` is still the documented default in `worktree-naming.sh:13`, `README.md:115`, and `README.md:125`, and the only documented way back out is a manual `git config speckit.worktreeBase <abs>`; the changelog even advertises "Unset the config to return to the in-checkout `.worktrees` layout" as a supported action. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh:13] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/changelog/v1.5.2.0.md:29]

Restoring "the reaper's daemon handling" therefore would not stop a single fsmonitor daemon. A fsmonitor reaper is new work, not a revert. [INFERENCE: from findings 1-2 plus `.skilled/bin/worktree-reaper.sh` now containing no `daemon`, `fsmonitor` or `orphan` token]

The auto-pin is recent: `f83952c3a94` (2026-09-11, "fix(sk-git): keep the reaper off live sessions and record autosync rewrites") introduced the config write-back, three weeks after `a69a621a39a` (2026-08-21) introduced the configurable base. The window between the two commits is exactly when a launch could have re-pinned `.worktrees` without any operator intent. [SOURCE: git log -S 'config speckit.worktreeBase "$WT_BASE_DIR"' -- .opencode/bin/worktree-session.sh .skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh]

The deleted logic never matched `git fsmonitor--daemon` at all. It enumerated `pgrep -f 'context-server\.js'` and skipped every process whose command line was not `*node*context-server.js*`, i.e. the retired spec-memory MCP daemons whose lease lived under a worktree DB dir. Two separate daemon populations were conflated in the packet's premise: sk-git/026 reaped MCP context-server daemons, and today's pile-up is git's own fsmonitor daemon. [SOURCE: git show 3c7c3f83874 -- .opencode/bin/worktree-reaper.sh]

The durable in-checkout default is re-created by the launch wrapper itself. `.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh:292-295` writes `speckit.worktreeBase = $WT_BASE_DIR` whenever the key is unset, and `_wn_base_dir()` falls back to `<toplevel>/.worktrees` when neither `SPECKIT_WORKTREE_BASE` nor the config key exists. So one launch without the env var converts the intended `~/worktrees/public` policy into a permanent `.worktrees` policy. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh:292] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh:71]

The live state matches the in-checkout default: `git config --get speckit.worktreeBase` is empty, `~/worktrees` exists but is empty, and 13 worktrees sit under `Public/.worktrees/` (087, 103, 140, 144, 145, 156, 197, 216, 217, 218, 219, 230, 231). The empty `~/worktrees` directory is the residue of the relocation, not of a live policy. [SOURCE: ls -d .worktrees/*, this session] [SOURCE: ls -la ~/worktrees, this session]

The reaper's daemon handling was deleted by `3c7c3f83874` (2026-09-03, "refactor(runtime): remove the memory launcher, plugin, hooks and the tool-ownership commit gate"), not by the `.opencode` → `.skilled` source-root move. That commit removed the `--reap-daemons` flag, the `_daemon_worktree_path_from_cmdline()` and `_daemon_cmdline_is_orphan()` helpers, the whole "5. ORPHAN DAEMON REPORTING" block, and the closing `orphan daemon candidates` log line from `.opencode/bin/worktree-reaper.sh`. [SOURCE: git show 3c7c3f83874 -- .opencode/bin/worktree-reaper.sh]

`--ipc-threads=8` in every live process is git's own compiled default, not this repo's configuration: `static int fsmonitor__ipc_threads = 8;` is the default for `fsmonitor.ipcthreads`, and this checkout sets no `fsmonitor.*` key at all. The argument is how the daemon re-execs itself into `run`, so it carries no signal about repo config. [SOURCE: builtin/fsmonitor--daemon.c:35-52] [SOURCE: git config --show-origin --get-regexp, iteration 1]

`git fsmonitor--daemon stop` sends `quit` and then polls `fsmonitor_ipc__get_state()` every 50 ms in an unbounded `while` loop. On a daemon that will not answer, the stop command itself hangs — exactly the observed behaviour where `stop` had to be killed after 15 seconds. [SOURCE: builtin/fsmonitor--daemon.c:88-101]

Because the Darwin health thread is a no-op and no idle exit exists, a daemon cannot retire itself. The 08:51:33 daemon (PID 17228) vanishing at 09:17:59 and being replaced by PID 18482 within a second therefore points at a signal or a crash, not at a timeout — the replacement is exactly what a client-start after a dead socket looks like. [INFERENCE: from findings 4-5] [SOURCE: specs/sk-git/035-fsmonitor-daemon-and-worktree-relocation-regression/scratch/findings.md]

Each blocked client holds one of the 8 IPC workers. Once the pool is saturated the daemon also stops answering `status` and `stop`, which is why the whole checkout looks frozen instead of one command looking slow, and why killing the daemon was the only thing that released the hook. [INFERENCE: from findings 2 and 6-7]

Event overload is the trigger, not the defect. A checkout with roughly 570k files plus roughly 2M under `.worktrees/`, with 93 `node_modules` trees, is a plausible way to lose or coalesce a cookie's FSEvents delivery under concurrent installs; the unbounded wait is what turns that dropped event into a 30-minute hang. [INFERENCE: from findings 6-8 and the packet's file census] [SOURCE: specs/sk-git/035-fsmonitor-daemon-and-worktree-relocation-regression/scratch/findings.md]

On macOS the health thread is a complete no-op: `fsm_health__ctor()`, `fsm_health__loop()` and `fsm_health__stop_async()` all return immediately, so the daemon does not monitor its own listener, does not detect a stalled FSEvents stream, and never shuts itself down on health grounds. [SOURCE: compat/fsmonitor/fsm-health-darwin.c:1-28] [SOURCE: compat/fsmonitor/fsm-health.h]

The 2.50.1 manual documents exactly four subcommands (`start`, `run`, `stop`, `status`) and describes the daemon as "a long running process used to watch a single working directory". It documents no idle timeout, no lifetime bound, no self-exit and no TTL. [SOURCE: man git-fsmonitor--daemon, Git 2.50.1.428.g0e8243]

The client side has no deadline either. `ipc_client_send_command_to_connection()` writes the command, flushes, then calls `read_packetized_to_strbuf(connection->fd, answer, PACKET_READ_GENTLE_ON_EOF | PACKET_READ_GENTLE_ON_READ_ERROR)` with no `poll()` and no timeout, so only EOF or a read error unblocks it. That is the exact frame the packet's `sample 28423` showed. The 10 ms `poll()` in the same file belongs to the server's `worker_thread__wait_for_io_start`, not to the client's reply read. [SOURCE: compat/simple-ipc/ipc-unix-socket.c:192-220] [SOURCE: compat/simple-ipc/ipc-unix-socket.c:440-506]

The cookie handshake is an acknowledged infinite wait. Every query other than `quit` creates a cookie file inside the watched tree, then blocks in `while (cookie->result == FCIR_INIT) pthread_cond_wait(...)`. The source comment says outright: "Technically, this is an infinite wait (well, unless another thread sends us an abort). I'd like to change this to use `pthread_cond_timedwait()` and return an error/timeout ... but we don't have that routine in our thread-utils." [SOURCE: builtin/fsmonitor--daemon.c:198-212]

The only timeout anywhere in the daemon's lifecycle is `fsmonitor.starttimeout` (default 60 s), and it bounds startup only — how long `start` waits for the background daemon to reach `IPC_STATE__LISTENING`. Nothing bounds a request. [SOURCE: builtin/fsmonitor--daemon.c:38-61,1510]

Therefore the sustained hang is not a lock deadlock with two owners. It is an unbounded wait on both sides, reachable whenever the filesystem event for a cookie is never delivered to the daemon's listener thread: the daemon's worker parks forever, the client's read parks forever, and the only exit is the socket closing. [INFERENCE: from findings 6-7 plus the packet's 0 %-CPU sleep-state sample]

Upgrading is not the fix path: the 2.51.0, 2.52.0 and 2.53.0 release notes contain zero fsmonitor entries, so no announced change addresses the unbounded cookie wait or the client's unbounded read. [SOURCE: Documentation/RelNotes/2.51.0.adoc] [SOURCE: Documentation/RelNotes/2.52.0.adoc] [SOURCE: Documentation/RelNotes/2.53.0.adoc]

`generate-leaf-manifest.cjs:129` runs `spawnSync('git', ['check-ignore', '-z', '--stdin'], { cwd: top, input, encoding })` with no `timeout` and no `-c core.fsmonitor=false`. `check-ignore` reads the index, so it takes the fsmonitor IPC path that iteration 2 showed is unbounded on both sides. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/generate-leaf-manifest.cjs:129]

keyFindings.text: Daemon-to-worktree attribution cannot use the command line. Iteration 1's census shows every daemon runs exactly `fsmonitor--daemon run --detach --ipc-threads=8`, with no path in argv, so the retired MCP-style `ps`-cmdline matcher has no successor by inspection of argv alone. The identifying artifact is the socket each process holds open (`.git/fsmonitor--daemon.ipc`, per worktree), which `lsof` resolves to a path. [SOURCE: ps -Ao pid,lstart,command, iteration 1] [SOURCE: specs/sk-git/035-fsmonitor-daemon-and-worktree-relocation-regression/scratch/findings.md]
sources: Iteration 1 process census and iteration 2 lifecycle findings

keyFindings.text: Prevention invariant: no fsmonitor daemon may outlive its worktree, and no automated git call may wait without a ceiling. Enforcement points are stop-before-`git worktree remove`, a stray-daemon reap in the doctor and after each removal, and a wedge probe that runs a bounded index read and restarts the daemon on timeout. [INFERENCE: findings 2, 7, 8]
sources: Iteration 1 process census and iteration 2 lifecycle findings

keyFindings.text: Q5 answer, ranked: the safe default is fsmonitor ON, but only with three preconditions — worktrees outside the checkout, automation opted out and time-bounded, and a daemon reaper that guarantees no daemon outlives its worktree. Without all three, fsmonitor OFF for the main checkout (via `extensions.worktreeConfig` plus `git config --worktree core.fsmonitor false`) is safer than an immortal daemon, because the main checkout is where index-reading automation runs and a wedge there stops pushes. The relocation is a prerequisite in either branch, not the alternative. [INFERENCE: iterations 1-2 findings]
sources: Iteration 1 process census and iteration 2 lifecycle findings

keyFindings.text: Recovery must escalate past `stop`. Since `git fsmonitor--daemon stop` sends `quit` and then polls forever on a wedged daemon, any reaper has to bound the stop (for example 5 s) and then send SIGTERM, then SIGKILL — the same escalation the operator performed by hand at 08:51. [INFERENCE: iteration 2 findings 4-5]

keyFindings.text: The highest-leverage single change is the hook path, not the daemon: the only user-visible damage was a 30-minute push, and a bounded, opted-out `check-ignore` turns a wedged daemon into a fast gate warning through the fallback that already exists. Daemon reaping and relocation then remove the recurrence rather than the symptom. [INFERENCE: findings 2-3 plus the packet's symptom record]

keyFindings.text: The hooks are machine-wide: `core.hooksPath` is `~/.config/git/hooks`, every entry is a symlink into `.skilled/scripts/git-hooks`, and the skill gate is skippable only by `SPECKIT_SKIP_PREPUSH_SKILL_GATE=1`. A timeout in this repo's scripts therefore fixes every machine checkout that trusts repo hooks, and leaving it unfixed leaves every one of them able to hang. [SOURCE: ~/.config/git/hooks/pre-push:425]

keyFindings.text: The same function's fallback cannot rescue a hang: `if (res.error || (res.status !== 0 && res.status !== 1))` requires a returned result, and a blocked `spawnSync` never returns. Adding `timeout` is therefore sufficient to make the existing fallback reachable — the repair is one option object, not a redesign. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/generate-leaf-manifest.cjs:136]

ruledOutDirections.text: "A repo commit reverted the relocated worktree base." Ruled out: the key is local config; the only repo-side actor is the wrapper's write-back.
"An operator shell command unset it and is recoverable from this shell's history." No hit in `~/.zsh_history`; the unset, if manual, happened in another session or before history rotation.

"The `.opencode` → `.skilled` move removed the daemon handling." Ruled out: `git log -S daemon` puts the deletion in `3c7c3f83874`, and the move commit `330427cf308` is the only commit touching the current path.
Git-config provenance for `speckit.worktreeBase`: `.git/config` is not versioned, so the exact unset action is unrecoverable from the repository. Recorded as an explicit UNKNOWN rather than guessed.

"`--ipc-threads=8` is a repo or Apple-specific tuning knob that might itself deadlock." Ruled out as a repo cause: 8 is the compiled default of `fsmonitor.ipcthreads`, and the repo sets no `fsmonitor.*` key. It remains a risk multiplier, not a root cause.
"A git upgrade fixes it." Ruled out for 2.51-2.53 by their release notes; the source comment in 2.50.1 states the timed wait was not implemented.
"The daemon exits on its own after idle time, so leaks are self-limiting." Ruled out: no idle mechanism exists, and the Darwin health thread is a no-op.
Locating a Darwin health-check policy: the implementation is an empty stub, so there is no policy to read. The daemon's own liveness is explicitly unmonitored on macOS.

"Disable fsmonitor everywhere." Rejected as the default rather than ruled out as an option: it discards a measured benefit on a 570k-file checkout, and per-worktree config gives the same safety with a narrower blast radius.
"Match daemons by command line." Ruled out by finding 7: argv is identical for every daemon.
"Rely on `git fsmonitor--daemon stop` in a reaper." Ruled out by iteration 2: stop hangs on exactly the daemon a reaper needs to remove.
"Restore the reaper's daemon handling." Ruled out by iteration 1: that code targeted MCP context-server daemons and the reaper now promises never to signal a process.
Measuring status latency with and without fsmonitor: every such command can write the index, which is a repository write outside this lineage's authority. Deferred with the reason recorded.
